text:
maya: FYI last night's telemetry recompute consumed ~2.3x our budgeted spot hours. I stopped the job. We need a short policy for cost cutoffs and partial recomputes.

sam: Can you paste the job id and the exact command?

maya: job id backfill-2026-03-10-42, triggered by scheduler v2. Command: `/run recompute --start=2026-03-01 --end=2026-03-10 --shards=200`

leo: Quick thought: we should add an early-exit cost cap per-run, e.g., `max_spot_hours` and `max_token_count`. Prevent runaway.

anita: SRE prefers a pre-run simulation estimate based on cardinality + avg tokens. We can compute an estimated token-hours from a 1% sample.

maya: I ran a 1% sample on the same window, estimate SQL I used:
```sql
select count(*) as rows, avg(tokens) as avg_tokens
from telemetry.events
where ts between '2026-03-01' and '2026-03-10'
```
(sample returned avg_tokens=142. Estimated token-hours ~ 18k) :eyes:

sam: We should expose that estimator in Console as a pre-flight check and show 'estimated cost' and 'SLA impact' before you press run.

leo: Operational options to consider: (1) priority lanes (critical customers first), (2) sample recompute then escalate to full only if regression detected, (3) partial-window recompute with sliding windows.

maya: Also routing policy: low-priority backfills go to cheaper preemptible pools or dedicated low-cost clusters, and high-priority go to reserved capacity. Need per-customer quota enforcement.

anita: Backstops we need: if `actual_spot_hours > budget_threshold` then auto-pause + notify on-call + create an incident ticket. Partial results should be committed so we don't lose progress.

deploy-bot: scheduled-maintenance: maintenance window tonight 02:00-05:00 UTC, will block spot launches in eu-west-1 :warning:

sam: Proposal for Console knobs: `max_estimated_hours`, `max_actual_hours`, `priority_tier`. Default suggestion: `max_estimated_hours=100h`, `max_actual_hours=200h`, `priority_tier=normal`.

maya: For windows older than 30d default sampling rate = 10%. For windows <7d allow full recompute but require an approval checkbox.

leo: From runtime: implement streaming-commit for aggregates so partial results are visible and safe to stop. That way we can pause without losing all progress.

anita: Runbook (short):
1) Check estimator & sample results
2) Check shard failure rates and recent spot events
3) If paused, either increase `max_actual_hours` + add approval, or reduce scope and resume with `--resume-from=shardX`

sam: UX: display `expected ETA`, `cost burn rate`, and a big red indicator when approaching `max_actual_hours`. Add a one-click `escalate to ops` that opens a prefilled ticket.

maya: Can someone own an RFC? I'll draft a short policy doc. Assign: @sam for Console changes, @leo for runtime/streaming, @anita for automation/runbook.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll take Console. I'll add mockups to the runway board and wire up estimator API.

leo: I'll prototype streaming-commit by EOD tomorrow. Kernel+KV cache changes ETA ~2w.

anita: I'll add automatic pause + pager rule and log per-backfill cost metrics so we can do chargeback analysis.

maya: Follow-ups: 1) sam create Console checklist 2) leo add sample estimator API 3) anita add automation + pager 4) maya draft RFC. I'll tag product.

frank: frank (product): Noted. Product will review RFC; we need SLA gating and product-level approval for >500h runs.

ops-bot: backfill-2026-03-10-42 status: paused by operator maya at 2310123465. Estimated consumed: 124h spot.

maya: Thanks all — let's sync briefly tomorrow 09:30 UTC to finalize knobs and runbook.
